item.title: PhD candidate in biology — theoretical and statistical modeling (m/f/x)
item.description:
Institution: Faculty of Biology

Remuneration: TV-L E13

Application deadline: 2025-12-15T22:59:18+00:00

Job Details:

About us:

<p>In the Statistical Genetics group at LMU Munich we develop and analyze probabilistic models for evolutionary processes and ecological interactions. Based on such explicit models we develop computational methods for statistical data analyses in population genetics and evolutionary genomics. Here we offer a PhD position supervised by <a href="https://evol.bio.lmu.de/_statgen/">Prof. Dirk Metzler</a> in a joint project with Dr. Luisa Pallares (MPI Tübingen) on the <a href="https://g-evol.uni-muenster.de/newprojects/projectpagenew/#AnkerNoise">evolution of transcriptional variability and its role in adaptation and evolutionary innovation</a>. The project is part of the DFG priority program "<a href="https://g-evol.uni-muenster.de/">Genomic Basis of Evolutionary Innovations</a>“, in which we collaborate with many researchers at LMU and other German and international universities and research institutions.</p>

Your qualifications:

<ul> <li> <p>You have completed or will soon complete a Master’s degree in a field related to biology, bioinformatics, statistics or mathematics.</p> </li> <li> <p>Of advantage is knowledge and experience in:</p> <p>o   mathematical modeling in evolutionary genomics and transcriptomics</p> <p>o   stochastic modeling of network interactions</p> <p>o   applying and extending statistical methods like GLMs and mixed-effect models</p> <p>o   phylogenetic methods</p> <p>o   programming, e.g. in R, python or C/C++</p> <p>o   theoretical evolutionary biology and population genetics</p> <p>o   working on Linux servers and with software like LaTeX and git</p> </li> <li> <p>You have good communication skills in English.</p> </li> <li> <p>You are highly motivated to work in a team and independently according to best scientific standards within an international and collaborative research environment, and enthusiastic about learning new methods and developing independent research expertise.<br/><br/></p> </li> </ul>

Benefits:

<ul> <li>Being part of a large network of researchers in <a href="https://g-evol.uni-muenster.de/">genome evolution</a></li> <li>Working at the LMU Munich, one of Germany’s and Europe’s top universities</li> <li>A supportive mentorship environment</li> <li>Employment according to the German public service pay agreement, including health insurance, 30 days of vacation per year, pension contributions, and other social security benefits.</li> <li>In addition, you can benefit from the various <a href="https://www.lmu.de/en/about-lmu/working-at-lmu/additional-services/corporate-benefits/">LMU corporate benefits</a></li> <li>Remuneration depending on qualifications and experience according to <a href="https://oeffentlicher-dienst.info/c/t/rechner/tv-l/allg?id=tv-l-2025&matrix=1">TV-L E13</a></li> </ul>

Contact: <p>Please send your application letter including a letter of motivation, CV and scans of degrees/certificates,  transcripts of your university education, and links to thesis, publications and other research output (e.g. git repositories) all in one pdf, by 15th of December via e-mail to <a href="mailto:metzler@bio.lmu.de">Prof. Dr. Dirk Metzler</a></p>

item.title: Postdoctoral researcher in data science or statistics (m/f/x)
item.description:
Institution: Faculty of Mathematics, Informatics and Statistics

Remuneration: TV-L E14

Application deadline: 2025-12-15T22:59:00+00:00

Job Details:

About us:

<p>The department of Statistics at Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München has a vacancy for a postdoctoral position in statistics and data science at the Chair of Applied Statistics in Social Sciences, Economics and Business. The team works on applied statistics in the field of Economics, Business Administration, Social and Political Sciences. Our research interests lie in the field of statistical network data analyses, data driven conflict and peace research, statistical modelling and quantification of uncertainty in machine learning</p>

Your qualifications:

<p>You have an excellent doctorate in statistics or data science, very good analytical skills, a high level of commitment, very good knowledge of English, the ability to work in a team and an independent approach to work.</p>

Benefits:

<p>We offer you an interesting and responsible position. Your workplace is centrally located in Munich and is easily accessible by public transport.<br /> The position is strictly limited in time from 15 April 2026 to 30 September 2026. Remuneration will be made, according to the relevant qualifications, on <a href="https://www.tdl-online.de/fileadmin/downloads/TV-L/TV-L_Anlagen/TV-L_Anlage_B_g%C3%BCltig_ab_01.02.2025.pdf">TV-L E14</a>.</p>

Contact: <p>We look forward to receiving your application by email (one PDF file, maximum 5 MB) with the usual documents (cover letter, resume, transcripts, list of publications and two letters of recommendation) <strong>by December 15, 2025</strong>, to <a href="mailto:goeran.kauermann@lmu.de">goeran.kauermann@lmu.de</a></p> <p>Prof. Dr. Göran Kauermann<br /> Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München,<br /> Department of Statistics</p>

item.title: Doctoral Researcher in the field of fluvial Geomorphology (m/f/x)
item.description:
Institution: Faculty of Geosciences

Remuneration: TV-L E13

Application deadline: 2026-01-31T22:59:34+00:00

Job Details:

About us:

<p>In the research group for Sedimentology and Earth Surface Processes, we develop quantitative constraints on the physical and chemical processes that control the evolution of landscapes, the erosion, transport, and deposition of sediments, and the global fluxes of dissolved solutes and carbon. To this end, we combine field observations, analogue experiments, geochronological methods, and geochemical analyses of sediment, soil, and water. Part of the Faculty for Geosciences, the research group is embedded in an environment with a broad range of expertise from geology and geophysics to paleontology, mineralogy, and physical geography.</p>

Your qualifications:

<ul> <li>A master's degree in Earth Science, Geology, Hydrology or similar (to be completed at the latest by the time of assuming the position)</li> <li>A high level of competence in oral and written English</li> <li>Independent, structured, and solution-oriented thinking</li> <li>Creativity and motivation to develop physical experiments and digital solutions for data acquisition and analysis</li> <li>Willingness to travel internationally including carrying out a research stay at the University of Utrecht, attending conferences in Europe and in the USA, and – optionally – participating in remote field\-work in Bolivia and Brazil</li> </ul>

Benefits:

<ul> <li>Wide range of stimulating activities in an ambitious and research-oriented team</li> <li>Salary at 75% of <a href="https://www.tdl-online.de/fileadmin/downloads/TV-L/TV-L_Anlagen/Allgemeine_Entgelttabelle__Anlage_B___g%C3%BCltig_ab_01.12.2022.pdf">TV-L</a> E13 and 30 days paid vacation</li> <li>Flexible working hours</li> <li>A family-friendly working environment in the center of Munich</li> <li>Further training opportunities through the <a href="https://www.lmu.de/de/die-lmu/arbeiten-an-der-lmu/wissenschaftlicher-nachwuchs/qualifizierung-und-entwicklung/">LMU Qualifications program</a></li> <li>Support for international students in relocating to Munich through the <a href="https://www.lmu.de/de/die-lmu/arbeiten-an-der-lmu/zusaetzliche-angebote/lmu-gateway/">LMU Gateway service</a></li> </ul>

Contact: <p>Inquiries prior to the application deadline can be directed to <a href="mailto:a.bufe@lmu.de">a.bufe@lmu.de</a>.</p> <p>To apply, please submit the following documents in English language, compiled into a single PDF file, to <a href="mailto:a.bufe@lmu.de">a.bufe@lmu.de</a> by <strong>January 31th 2026</strong>:</p> <ul> <li>Cover letter explaining your achievements and your motivation to do your PhD as part of the project FloW (max. two pages)</li> <li>A short CV (max two pages)</li> <li>An example of your writing (e.g. your bachelor´s or master´s thesis or a paper without co-authors)</li> <li>Contact information of two references</li> <li>Copies of your bachelor´s and master´s degrees with transcripts (If your master´s degree is not completed by the time of application, you can upload the latest available transcripts. You will require a completed master´s degree at the latest when assuming the position at LMU.)</li> </ul>

item.title: Research/Teaching Assistant (PhD Candidate) in Financial and Sustainability Reporting (m/f/x)
item.description:
Institution: Faculty of Business Administration - Munich School of Management

Remuneration: TV-L E13

Application deadline: 2026-01-15T22:59:00+00:00

Job Details:

About us:

<p>Our highly motivated team, led by Prof. Dr. Thorsten Sellhorn, is based in the city of Munich. We are part of the transregional DFG project <a href="https://www.accounting-for-transparency.de/">TRR 266 <em>Accounting for Transparency</em></a> and the <a href="http://www.srnav.com/">Sustainability Reporting Navigator</a> (SRN) team, and explore research questions related to financial and sustainability reporting:</p> <ul> <li>The SRN provides an open-science resource that enables firms, their stakeholders, and the public to navigate the evolving field of sustainability reporting.</li> <li>The TRR 266 is a trans-regional Collaborative Research Center funded by the German Research Foundation (DFG). Our team of more than 100 dedicated researchers examines how accounting and sustainability reporting affect firm and regulatory transparency, and how regulation and transparency impact our economy and society. We help develop effective regulation for corporate transparency, and we ensure the transparency of our own research.</li> </ul> <p>Please visit our <a href="https://www.rwp.bwl.uni-muenchen.de/index.html">website for further information</a>.</p>

Your qualifications:

<ul> <li>You have completed (or are near completion of) a Master’s degree in business administration, economics, or a related field of study – ideally specializing in accounting, finance, machine learning, and/or sustainability management.</li> <li>You have the skills and motivation to work in the above research fields.</li> <li>You have acquired empirical skills (ideally, including AI-based natural language processing approaches) as well as substantive expertise in accounting theory and practice, through either specialization in Bachelor's and/or Master's programs, topical and methodological theses, or relevant internships.</li> <li>You have very good analytical skills, German and English language skills (both at C1-levels), and you are a reliable and helpful team player.</li> <li>An independent way of working and a high level of commitment are also welcome.</li> </ul>

Benefits:

<ul> <li>PhD candidates will be enrolled in the LMU Munich School of Management’s Master in Business Research (MBR) program, a structured doctoral curriculum that provides rigorous methodological training, subject-specific courses, and professional development modules.</li> <li>Your workplace is centrally located in Munich at LMU’s main campus, right next to the <em>Englischer Garten</em>. Our <a href="https://www.som.lmu.de/de/forschung/accounting-taxation/index.html">Accounting and Taxation cluster</a> works internationally in an open and cooperative atmosphere.</li> <li>Our research in the fields of financial and sustainability accounting and reporting, corporate governance and auditing, financial analysis, valuation, and taxation contributes evidence-based solutions to practical problems.</li> <li>This role offers intellectual stimulation and an opportunity to contribute as a member to the highly topical research agendas of the <a href="https://www.accounting-for-transparency.de/"><em>TRR 266 Accounting for Transparency</em></a> and the <a href="https://sustainabilityreportingnavigator.com/">Sustainability Reporting Navigator</a> – allowing you to delve deep into new, exciting areas of expertise and to develop valuable research skills. We offer payment according to <a href="https://www.tdl-online.de/fileadmin/downloads/TV-L/TV-L_Anlagen/Allgemeine_Entgelttabelle__Anlage_B___g%C3%BCltig_ab_01.12.2022.pdf">TVLE13</a> There is the possibility of partly working from home. Applications by women are welcome.</li> </ul> <p>Please find information about LMU career opportunity support services <a href="https://www.lmu.de/en/about-lmu/working-at-lmu/academic-careers/index.html">here</a>.</p>

Contact: <p>We look forward to receiving your application. Please send your documents as a single PDF file to Prof. Dr. Thorsten Sellhorn (<a href="mailto:sellhorn@lmu.de">sellhorn@lmu.de</a>), with a copy to <a href="mailto:rwp@som.lmu.de">rwp@som.lmu.de</a> (Melanie von Franckenstein) <strong>no later than 15.01.2026.</strong></p>

item.title: PhD candidate in Geosciences - Volcanology (m/f/x)
item.description:
Institution: Faculty of Geosciences

Remuneration: TV-L E13

Application deadline: 2025-12-15T22:59:11+00:00

Job Details:

About us:

<p>The Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences at LMU covers the entire spectrum of geoscientific disciplines, including geology, paleontology and geobiology, magmatic petrology and volcanology, geomaterials and geophysics. In addition, there is close cooperation with the geoscience-oriented state collections and the geoscience subjects at the Technical University of Munich. This constellation, which is unique in Germany, is predestined for strongly interdisciplinary research and teaching in order to achieve and communicate in-depth scientific knowledge of planet Earth and its interrelationships in time, space and the future.<br /> The Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (LMU) is seeking to fill a doctoral position in the field of magmatic petrology and volcanology as part of a DFG-funded Emmy Noether project starting in January 2026 (headed by Dr. Edgar Zorn). The project aims to investigate compaction processes of volcanic loose materials and their effects on surface deformations, changes in the physical and mechanical properties of loose materials, as well as their failure strengths and the stability of volcano flanks. The approach is interdisciplinary and specifically combines methods from field geology, remote sensing, laboratory-based petrophysics and numerical modelling.</p>

Your qualifications:

<ul> <li>A master's degree in geosciences, geology, geophysics or a related subject</li> <li>High motivation for planning and carrying out independent research work as well as an independent, structured and responsible approach to work</li> <li>Basic knowledge of geoscientific and geospatial data processing is required</li> <li>Expertise and project experience in one or more of the following fields: volcanology, satellite remote sensing, photogrammetry, petrology/petrophysics</li> <li>Fluency in spoken and written English is required</li> <li>Experience with programming languages is desirable (e.g. Matlab, Python)</li> <li>Experience in scientific work in the field and/or in the laboratory is desirable</li> <li>Experience with drones and an EU licence (A1/A3) is desirable</li> <li>Experience in the publication of scientific literature is desirable</li> </ul>

Benefits:

<ul> <li>Collaboration in a highly topical, socially relevant research project in the field of volcanology</li> <li>Opportunity for independent research, publication and further scientific qualification</li> <li>Flexible working conditions and involvement in the research and teaching activities of the Chair of Magmatic Petrology and Volcanology</li> <li>State-of-the-art workplace equipment and unique geoscience laboratories</li> <li>The position is for a fixed term of three years, with remuneration depending on qualifications up to E13 <a href="https://www.tdl-online.de/fileadmin/downloads/TV-L/TV-L_Anlagen/Allgemeine_Entgelttabelle__Anlage_B___g%C3%BCltig_ab_01.12.2022.pdf">TV-L</a></li> </ul>

Contact: <p>Please send your application documents (including a letter of motivation, CV, copies of degrees/certificates)</p> <p>by <strong>15th December 2025</strong> via e-mail (ideally as a single PDF attachment including all documents) to <a href="mailto:e.zorn@lmu.de"><strong>e.zorn@lmu.de</strong></a>.</p> <p>Interviews are expected to take place online in January 2026. Applications without a final degree certificate for the Master's Programme can be considered provided that the graduation criteria have already been met.</p>

item.title: Seismologist at PhD candidate level (m/f/x)
item.description:
Institution: Faculty of Geosciences

Remuneration: TV-L E13

Application deadline: 2025-12-31T22:59:40+00:00

Job Details:

About us:

<p>The Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences and the Geophysical Observatory of the Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München are leading geophysical research institutions in Europe as well as worldwide. We are seeking a Seismologist at PhD candidate level in Munich and our Observatory in Fürstenfeldbruck for the DFG funded project KAROS - Investigation of the Kefalonia Fault Zone using seismic wavefield analyses: seismicity, amphibious array measurements, local gradients, and rotations.</p> <p>KAROS is part of the DFG priority program DEFORM which focuses on plate deformation and geohazards in the eastern margin of the Adriatic plate. It is a joint project from LMU Munich, CAU Kiel and GEOMAR Kiel. The focus area of KAROS is the Kefalonia Transform Fault Zone (KTFZ), one of the most active strike-slip fault zones in Europe.</p> <p>With a first of its kind amphibious experiment (involving off- and on-shore seismic stations) KAROS aims at gaining new insights about the crustal deformation and structural properties of the KTFZ. Direct and array derived wavefield gradient observations with gradiometry and Helmholtz tomography using ambient noise and earthquake data will be used to improve our knowledge about the local shear-wave velocity structure and the seismicity along the KTFZ.</p>

Your qualifications:

<ul> <li>MSc in an Earth science related topic</li> <li>Ability to work independently and within a team</li> <li>Attention to detail and high level of critical thinking</li> <li>Experience with seismological field work is highly appreciated</li> <li>Experience in Python programming is an advantage</li> <li>Proficiency in English language is essential</li> </ul>

Benefits:

<ul> <li>LMU offers an interdisciplinary environment with excellent opportunities for further training and development</li> <li>Fixed term contract for three years 75%</li> <li><a href="https://www.tdl-online.de/fileadmin/downloads/TV-L/TV-L_Anlagen/Allgemeine_Entgelttabelle__Anlage_B___g%C3%BCltig_ab_01.12.2022.pdf">TV-L</a> E 13</li> <li>LMU Munich is interested in increasing the number of female employees and encourages women to apply</li> <li>Flexible, family friendly working time models (e. g. Home Office ) in the center of the attractive and vibrant city of Munich close to the Alpes</li> </ul>

Contact: <p>Complete applications must include a motivation letter (max. one page), CV, and two recommendation letters.</p> <p><strong>Deadline for applications is 31.12.2025.</strong></p> <p>Please send your application to: <a href="mailto:felix.bernauer@lmu.de">felix.bernauer@lmu.de</a></p> <p>Dr. Felix Bernauer<br /> Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences<br /> LMU Munich<br /> Theresienstrasse 41<br /> 80333 Munich<br /> Germany</p>

item.title: PhD Position in Large-Scale Galaxy Clustering and Higher-Order Statistics (m/f/x)
item.description:
Institution: Faculty of Physics

Remuneration: TV-L E13

Application deadline: 2025-12-15T22:59:00+00:00

Job Details:

About us:

<p>We invite applications for a PhD position in observational and theoretical cosmology at the newly established Emmy Noether Research Group of Jiamin Hou at LMU.</p> <p>The Emmy Noether group at LMU will focus on exploiting the next generation of galaxy surveys to study the large-scale structure of the Universe with unprecedented precision. We are particularly interested in developing and applying higher-order clustering statistics to extract cosmological information from ongoing and upcoming galaxy surveys. These methods will provide complementary constraints on cosmological parameters, tests of fundamental physics, and of signatures of early-Universe physics.</p>

Your qualifications:

<ul> <li>You have completed, or are close to completing, an M.Sc. degree in physics, astronomy, cosmology, or a closely related field.</li> <li>You have prior research experience in at least one of the following areas: large-scale structure, cosmological data analysis, statistical methods in astrophysics, galaxy surveys, or related theoretical and computational fields.</li> <li>Experience with scientific programming (e.g. Python, C/C++, Julia, or similar) is an advantage.</li> <li>You are a team player, motivated to contribute within an international and collaborative research environment, and enthusiastic about learning new methods and developing independent research expertise.</li> </ul>

Benefits:

<ul> <li>The position is expected to start in April 2026, with flexibility.A fully funded PhD position at LMU Munich within the Emmy Noether group of Jiamin Hou.</li> <li>Employment according to the German public service pay agreement, including health insurance, pension contributions, and other social security benefits.</li> <li>The opportunity to work at the forefront of cosmological research, with access to current and upcoming survey data (e.g., DESI, Euclid, Roman), and to collaborate with international survey teams.</li> <li>Optional participation in the structured graduate school program of the International Max Planck Research School (IMPRS), run jointly by LMU, the Max Planck Institutes for Astrophysics and Extraterrestrial Physics, and the European Southern Observatory.</li> <li>A supportive mentorship environment with opportunities for research visits, conference travel, and networking within the international cosmology community.</li> <li>A stimulating local community: LMU’s University Observatory is embedded in Munich’s strong astrophysics ecosystem, including the Max Planck Institutes for Astrophysics and Extraterrestrial Physics, ESO headquarters, TUM, and the DFG Cluster of Excellence <em>ORIGINS</em>.</li> <li>Company pension scheme</li> <li>Capital forming payments</li> <li>Compatibility between family and work: <ul> <li>Flexible work times</li> <li>Support by childcare (e.g. offer of vacations- and emergency childcare)</li> </ul> </li> <li>Development programs in all career steps</li> <li>Offer of health protecion activities</li> <li>Theater and culture: special events, discounts and flyers</li> <li>Mobility: jobtickets, charging stations for electric cars, and discounted membership by Share Now (Carsharing).</li> </ul>

Contact: <p>Please upload the following documents in electronic form (as a single PDF) to <a href="mailto:Jiamin.Hou@physik.uni-muenchen.de">Jiamin.Hou@physik.uni-muenchen.de</a>:</p> <ul> <li>A cover letter outlining your motivation and research interests</li> <li>A CV including names and contact details of at least two references</li> <li>Transcripts of your university education</li> <li>Links to theses, publications, or other research outputs</li> </ul> <p><strong>Application deadline is December 15, 2025</strong>.</p> <p>For inquiries about this position, please contact Jiamin Hou directly at <a href="mailto:Jiamin.Hou@physik.uni-muenchen.de">Jiamin.Hou@physik.uni-muenchen.de</a></p>
